## The three defects the controls caught that reading did not

Each was found by RUNNING something, not by review — which is this plan's thesis
applied to its own execution.

1. **`plan_extract` sub-key masking.** The sub-key pattern matches against
   `mask_inline_code(raw)`, where a backticked term is blanked to spaces — so the
   whitespace run after the colon greedily swallowed the entire FIRST backticked
   value. Every `touches:` list lost its first path and single-path lists came back
   EMPTY (13 of 31 issues), while `--strict` still reported `unparsed: []` and exit
   0. Same shape as #186 but reached by moved OFFSETS rather than captured masked
   text, so `_verbatim`'s fix did not cover it.
2. **`cmd_closable` dropped `close_reason`.** The bead projection discarded it
   before grouping, so the hoist-tombstone signal was invisible to
   `closable_candidates` NO MATTER HOW the predicate was written.
3. **A control that printed FAIL and exited 0.** A heredoc's exit status was never
   read, so the script fell through to its final `echo`. The control's own subject,
   reproduced inside the control.

## What plan-053 should pick up

- **The corpus is unmigrated.** 0 of 186 criteria outside this plan are in the
  clause grammar, so `recheck-criteria` is INCONCLUSIVE almost everywhere and maps
  to `warn` by design. Migrating even a handful of recent bundles would turn the
  re-check from a mechanism into a measurement.
- **`ownership-report` is REPORT-ONLY and partially circular** — it is generated by
  one of the five `plan_manager.py` writers it flags. Do not promote it to a gate
  without an independent measurement.
- **The run-record (#217) is the shared prerequisite** for both the recipe-row
  predicate and the criterion-re-check predicate. Neither is buildable without it.
- **#192 (structure-first plan DSL) now has four ad-hoc sub-keys behind it.**
  plan-052 shipped the third and fourth. A fifth is the point at which the general
  form should win.
